entities.summary:
The Battle of the Milvian Bridge was a pivotal event in the struggle for control of the Roman Empire, fought between the forces of Emperor Constantine I and the co-emperors Maxentius and Maxentius's father, Maxentius himself. This decisive battle, which took place on October 28, 312 AD, near the Milvian Bridge in Rome, marked a turning point in the history of the Western world. Constantine's victory not only secured his position as the sole ruler of the Western Roman Empire but also laid the groundwork for the rise of Christianity as the dominant faith in the Roman world. The legacy of the Battle of the Milvian Bridge can be seen in the establishment of Constantinople as the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire and the adoption of Christianity as the official state religion.

The battle itself was a fierce and bloody struggle, with both sides suffering heavy losses. Constantine's forces, led by his trusted generals, defeated the armies of Maxentius in a series of intense battles that raged across the Italian peninsula. The turning point of the battle came when Constantine's troops, who were largely composed of soldiers from the Eastern provinces, broke through the lines of the Roman legions and sent Maxentius's forces fleeing in disarray. The defeat of Maxentius marked the beginning of a new era in Roman history, one in which the Christian faith would come to play a dominant role.

The impact of the Battle of the Milvian Bridge can be seen in the subsequent conversion of Constantine to Christianity and the patronage he extended to the Church. The establishment of Constantinople as the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire also marked a significant shift in the balance of power in the Mediterranean world. The legacy of the battle can also be seen in the subsequent rise of Christianity as a dominant force in European society.
